claims.statement: F1: the suite guards against fixture rot and against unexpected blocking claims
claims.suggestion: keep the coverage guard and the unexpected-blocker check so a fixture cannot rot unwatched

claims.statement: F4: the reviewer body carries its read-only, scope and bounded-iteration discipline
claims.suggestion: restore the Read-only discipline, Scope discipline and budget sections in .opencode/agents/reviewer.md

claims.statement: F6: the fact-checker may only report evidence-backed findings — it must quit the fabrication mode measured in the RV-F12345 dry run (findings with no path:line, no quoted command output, and conditional 'passes if ...' verdicts)
claims.suggestion: restore the Evidence (binding) rules, the banned-phrasing list and the pre-return self-check in .opencode/agents/fact-checker.md

checks.pattern: Quote the bytes, never the impression
Assert only what you ran this session
Label the outcome by what the evidence shows

claims.statement: F7: the reviewer may not recompose the runner's output — it reads the envelope out of the file the runner wrote and copies the verdict-bearing fields (task_id, role, status, findings) unaltered, never inventing a finding or confirming a claim it did not see, and it must not drop the findings[] key
claims.suggestion: restore the Verbatim discipline (binding) section in .opencode/agents/reviewer.md

checks.pattern: Use `--attest`, which is why it exists
Never alter a string inside `artifact` or `findings`
If your message has no `findings` key

claims.statement: F8: the reviewer's echo burden is mechanically reduced - --attest writes the full envelope to a file and prints a short attestation that --verify re-hashes, so a paraphrased envelope is detectable rather than merely forbidden; because a bounded reviewer drops the attestation's non-canonical keys and re-words its summary while copying task_id/role/status/findings exactly, --verify resolves a missing artifact pointer from task_id and reports a re-worded summary in notes rather than failing a correct audit
claims.suggestion: restore the --attest/--verify path in scripts/review-gate.mjs, its pinned contract in scripts/review-gate.test.mjs, and the --attest instruction in .opencode/agents/reviewer.md

checks.pattern: artifact.sha256: not a 64-character lowercase hex digest

claims.statement: F9: an attestation artifact is immutable evidence - if the target already exists with differing content, --attest refuses (status blocked, summary naming --force) rather than silently invalidating the attestation that already points at its hash; --force overwrites deliberately
claims.suggestion: restore the existence check and the usageEnvelope refusal in scripts/review-gate.mjs, and the artifact immutability cases in scripts/review-gate.test.mjs

checks.pattern: refuses to overwrite a differing artifact without --force
the refused artifact is left untouched

advisories.issue: the frontmatter denies action 'execute', which is not a permission action in OpenCode 2.0.26 — the shell tool maps to 'shell' and write/patch map to 'edit' (see $A/oh/A$ in the opencode build) — so this rule is inert. The enforced read-only guarantee is 'edit: deny'; shell remains allowed and must stay allowed, because the reviewer runs check commands to gather evidence.
advisories.suggestion: drop the inert 'execute' rule (the same inert rule is in .opencode/agents/fact-checker.md) and, if command execution really must be forbidden, say 'shell: deny' — but then the reviewer can no longer run scripts such as scripts/review-gate.mjs, so 'edit: deny' plus the read-only discipline section is the workable guarantee
